content.text:
This is delavirdine, read region by region from the drawing.

- **Indole core:** The N-H sits at position 1. C2 carries the carbonyl. The benzene ring carries the NHSO2CH3 group at C5.
- **Linker:** The C2 carbonyl is an amide to a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen attaches to C2 of a pyridine.
- **Pyridine:** The ring nitrogen is next to C2. C3 carries an NH-isopropyl group.

Writing the SMILES:

CC(C)Nc1cccnc1N1CCN(CC1)C(=O)c1cc2cc(NS(C)(=O)=O)ccc2[nH]1

Checks:
- The indole is written as c1cc2cc(NS...)ccc2[nH]1. C2 is the attachment carbon, C3 is cH, and C3a is c2. After C3a comes C4 (cH), then C5 bearing the NHSO2Me, then C6 and C7 (cc), and finally C7a (c2) bonded to the [nH]. This matches the drawing.
- The pyridine is written as c1cccnc1N…, where c1 bears the NH-iPr, then three cH, then n, then the carbon bearing the piperazine. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)Nc1cccnc1N1CCN(CC1)C(=O)c1cc2cc(NS(C)(=O)=O)ccc2[nH]1
